## Military Politics A well-run military doesn't encourage factions in its ranks, but they form anyway wherever officers disagree. Across the [textlink="United Americas" link="CMUGuideLoreUA"]' militaries, from the [textlink="Colonial Marines" link="CMUGuideLoreUSCM"] (USCM) to the [textlink="Latin American Colonial Navy" link="CMUGuideLoreOrgLACN"] (LACN) and the rest of United Americas Allied Command (UAAC), three schools of thought dominate. Each has an official name, but servicemembers know them best by the bird nicknames that have been around for generations.
- [textlink="The Doves" link="CMUGuideLoreUADoves"]: the Hearts and Minds Movement (HMM), peacekeepers focused on humanitarian aid. - [textlink="The Hawks" link="CMUGuideLoreUAHawks"]: the Colonial Protection Organization (CPO), who seek to crush all resistance and win glory through victory. - [textlink="The Magpies" link="CMUGuideLoreUAMagpies"]: the Military Organization for Development and Innovation (MODI), opportunists tied to the corporations that arm the military.
Most servicemembers lean one way or another, and many officers' careers depend on which faction they keep close.
